title: Jephthah of Gilead

named.name: Gilead
named.label: right
named.site: the hill country east of the Jordan
named.note: The wooded highlands between the Yarmuk and the Arnon, settled by Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh. The Ammonites oppressed "all the Israelites on the other side of the Jordan in Gilead" for eighteen years (10:8).

named.name: Mizpah of Gilead
named.label: right
named.note: Israel camped at Mizpah facing the Ammonites (10:17). Jephthah was made leader here "before the LORD" (11:11), and here his daughter came out to meet him with tambourines (11:34). Probably the Mizpah or "watchtower" where Jacob and Laban made their covenant (Genesis 31:49).

named.name: Tob
named.label: right
named.note: Driven out by his half-brothers, Jephthah fled to the land of Tob, an Aramean region east of Gilead, where worthless men gathered around him (11:3). Tob later sent men to help the Ammonites against David (2 Samuel 10:6).

named.name: Rabbah
named.label: right
named.note: The capital of the Ammonites, not named in Judges. Today's Amman takes its name from Ammon.

named.name: Arnon
named.label: below
named.note: The deep gorge into the Salt Sea, the border of Moab. The Ammonite king claimed "from the Arnon to the Jabbok"; Jephthah answered that Israel took that land from Sihon king of the Amorites, not from Ammon or Moab (11:13, 18–22).

named.name: Jabbok
named.label: below
named.note: The northern limit of the land the Ammonite king claimed (11:13, 22).

named.name: Heshbon
named.label: left
named.note: The city of Sihon. "Israel lived in Heshbon… for three hundred years. Why did you not take them back during that time?" (11:26).

named.name: Jahaz
named.label: right
named.note: Sihon fought Israel at Jahaz and was defeated (11:20–21; Numbers 21:23).

named.name: Aroer
named.label: right
named.site: Arair, on the edge of the Arnon gorge
named.note: Aroer on the Arnon, one of the towns Israel had held for three hundred years (11:26). The Aroer of 11:33 is probably another town of that name near Rabbah (Joshua 13:25), shown as "Aroer near Rabbah."

named.name: Aroer near Rabbah
named.label: left
named.site: unknown; Khirbet Udena is one proposal
named.note: Jephthah struck the Ammonites "from Aroer to the vicinity of Minnith, as far as Abel-keramim," twenty cities (11:33). This Aroer is "near Rabbah" (Joshua 13:25).

named.name: Minnith
named.label: right
named.note: Known later for its wheat, traded at Tyre (Ezekiel 27:17).

named.name: Abel-keramim
named.label: right
named.note: "Meadow of vineyards," the limit of the victory (11:33).

named.name: Zaphon
named.label: left
named.note: The men of Ephraim crossed the Jordan to Zaphon to threaten Jephthah: "We will burn your house down on you" (12:1).

named.name: Fords of the Jordan
named.label: left
named.note: The Gileadites held the fords. Each fugitive was told to say "Shibboleth"; an Ephraimite said "Sibboleth," and was killed. 42,000 of Ephraim fell (12:5–6).

symbols.key: The Ammonites are subdued before Israel
"Shibboleth": 42,000 men of Ephraim fall at the fords

p: Before fighting, Jephthah sent the Ammonite king a history lesson (11:12–28): Israel came from Egypt to Kadesh, asked passage from Edom and Moab and was refused, went around their lands, and took the land "from the Arnon to the Jabbok" from Sihon king of the Amorites, who attacked them. It was not Ammon's land, and Israel had lived there three hundred years. "Let the LORD, the Judge, decide today."

The word means an ear of grain, or a flowing stream. Ephraimites west of the Jordan seem to have pronounced the sh as s, and could not hide their speech. The quarrel recalls Ephraim's complaint to Gideon (8:1–3); this time it ended in civil war, a first sign of the division that runs through the end of the book.
